scenes.say: Ever wonder why SQL joins trip up so many engineers? And what do those NULLs really tell you?

scenes.label: INNER
scenes.sub: Only rows with matching keys in both tables.
scenes.say: An inner join gives you just the rows where both tables have matching keys.
Left join keeps every row from the left table, filling in blanks with NULLs if there's no match. Right join does the same, but for the right table.

scenes.title: FULL JOIN Example
lines: $ SELECT * FROM a FULL JOIN b
scenes.say: A full join returns every row from both tables. If there's no match, you'll see NULLs in the missing columns.

scenes.question: What happens if you skip the ON clause?
scenes.right: You get a Cartesian product—every row from the first table paired with every row from the second. That can mean millions of rows by accident.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: forget the join condition, and you'll accidentally multiply your rows with a Cartesian product.
